summary: Postmortem follow-up for the 2027-11-22 inference degradation incident affecting Aurora's production inference. Root cause discussed as combination of inter-region network flaps and a missed autoscale trigger tied to a custom metric. Short-term mitigations: increase healthcheck cadence, add synthetic cache warmups, lower batch size for tail latency. Medium-term: pilot dedicated capacity with reserved GPUs and add alerting for inference queue depth and KV cache miss rate.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-25 15:00 PST — Duration: 54m — Attendees: Sam (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Omar (Redwood CSM), Lena (Aurora SRE), Marco (Aurora CTO), Arman (Aurora Platform), Sofia (Aurora PM)

[00:00] Sam: Okay thanks everyone for joining. we wanted to follow up from the outage on monday the 22nd, run through the postmortem, and make sure the mitigations we put in place are holding. also to map next steps for the dedicated pilot.

[00:18] Lena: Thanks Sam. yeah appreciate that. quick note, still seeing a small bump in tail latency at peak in prod, not nearly the same as last week but it's there.

[00:28] Priya: got it. we ran the initial traces you shared and there's two things that popped out for us — one was an inter-region network flap between eu-west-1 and us-west-2 that increased request retrying, and the other was an autoscale policy that didn't trigger because it was wired to a custom cpu metric that dropped during the incident.

[00:45] Marco: i want to be clear — our infra team didn't change the autoscale rule intentionally that day, there was a k8s operator bump the morning prior but we didn't think that would affect the metric stream.

[01:00] Priya: yeah we saw the operator deploy timestamp aligned with the metric gap. also the KV cache warm start was lower because a rolling deploy cleared the in-memory prefixes. combined, requests suddenly hit cold KV and the fallback routing attempted to reroute to different region nodes which then hit the network flap, increasing retries and queueing.

[01:22] Arman: when you say "KV cash" — sorry — "KV cache" — is the cache rebuilt synchronously on first token or do you have some background warm?

[01:30] Priya: currently it's lazy — first requests populate. for prod we recommended a synthetic warmup which we sketched in the postmortem doc, but that wasn't in place.

[01:45] Lena: we did add the temporary rule to reduce burst batch size and enabled the canary fallback earlier that day which helped a bit.

[02:00] Sam: good call. just to capture a clean root cause statement: the outage resulted from a combination of (1) inter-region network instability, (2) cache cold-start after rolling deploy, and (3) a misconfigured autoscale trigger tied to a non-robust metric. any objections to that framing?

[02:18] Marco: no, that's accurate.

[02:25] Sofia: i second that, add that our lack of synthetic warmup was a gap.

[02:35] Priya: moving to mitigations: short term we recommended — increase healthcheck cadence so region-level flaps are detected faster, add alert on inference queue depth and token generation retries, lower batch size for tail latency sensitive routes, and implement synthetic warmup traffic during deploys; medium-term: pilot Redwood Dedicated reserved pool to avoid cross-region routing for hot traffic, and add autoscale fallback to a secondary metric.

[03:05] Lena: can you walk through the dedicated pilot tradeoffs again? we worry about cost and overprovisioning.

[03:12] Sam: yeah absolutely. dedicated gives you a reserved GPU pool in-region so routing stays local; it reduces cross-region failovers and keeps model state warmed on a set of nodes. cost is higher but more predictable. for Aurora's peak pattern we estimate the dedicated pilot at 3x the on-demand hosted cost but 60% lower tail latency and simpler QC for compliant workloads.

[03:40] Marco: what's the rollback story if we see a performance regression on dedicated?

[03:45] Priya: we support canary routing and automatic fallback to hosted variants — so we can route a small percentage to the dedicated pool and measure. if signs degrade, we can shift back and we retain the same API and model versioning, so rollback is quick. there was a note in logs about some model kernel mismatch but that turned out to be a false positive — transcript may show "kernel missmatch" — those were just perf counters during heavy tail that didn't affect model correctness.

[04:18] Arman: you mentioned an autoscale fallback — how would that be implemented?

[04:25] Priya: simplest is run a dual-metric policy: primary metric cpu or token/s, secondary metric queue depth or inference latency P95. if primary metric stops emitting, the policy looks to secondary and triggers. we can also add a heartbeat from the k8s operator; that was missing.

[04:45] Sam: let's talk monitoring gaps. we saw there wasn't an alert for KV cache miss rate or cold start frequency, and there wasn't a historical baseline for prefix hit rates.

[04:58] Lena: we only had model-level telemetry, not cache-level. we'll add cache metrics in our next sprint.

[05:10] Priya: tactical remediation we did post-incident: 1) added queue-depth alert to prod, 2) lowered batch target on the worst-affected route from 32 -> 12, 3) deployed a small synthetic warmup job for staging and are rolling to prod as a canary, 4) patched the autoscale policy to include queue depth as a fallback. those changes are in prod but we're watching.

[05:40] Marco: we've seen improvement but still occasional spikes at 6pm PST. what's the hypothesized cause for the residual spikes?

[05:48] Priya: my hunch is partial warmup misses from long-tail user queries that don't hit common prefixes; also some regional DNS inconsistencies causing occasional routing to older nodes.

[06:05] Arman: can we get more detailed logs for the 6pm window? we can correlate with deploy times and internal batcher metrics.

[06:12] Sam: yes we'll share redacted logs. action: Sam to share logs and a trimmed timeline.

[06:20] Omar: quick question on security / compliance touches — do we need to update anything in the SOC2 docs for the dedicated pilot?

[06:27] Sam: good call. we'll include the dedicated topology and KMS flow in the pack Sam is sending, and include a note about audit log retention options for Dedicated and Private.

[06:38] Marco: one ask — can Redwood run the dedicated benchmark with our real tokenizer and request distribution? that was a big unknown for us.

[06:45] Priya: yes, we'll run with your tokenizer and a recorded traffic replay. we'll include KV cache warmup scenarios and compare P50/P95/P99 and cost delta.

[07:00] Sofia: what's the expected timeline for that benchmark?

[07:05] Priya: aim for 3 runs across representative times — i can get preliminary numbers by 2027-11-29.

[07:12] Marco: perfect.

[07:18] Lena: operationally we'll need a short window to grant limited staging VPC access for the run.

[07:25] Arman: i'll open a ticket after this call to grant that.

[07:32] Sam: excellent. i want to capture some long-term reliability improvements we recommended: pre-warm strategies, dual-metric autoscaling, per-route batch sizing, and synthetic traffic as part of deploy pipelines; also add retry budget enforcement and rate-limiting per-customer to avoid noisy-neighbor tail effects.

[08:00] Lena: retry budget enforcement — can Redwood enforce this at the platform layer?

[08:06] Priya: yes we have request-level throttles and token-based budgets. we can propose a guardrail configuration for Aurora and include it in the pilot.

[08:18] Marco: any concerns about correctness when lowering batch sizes? we've seen model throughput drop but we want tail latency.

[08:25] Priya: there's a tradeoff, yes. some of your high-throughput routes will cost more per token with smaller batches; we'll produce cost vs latency curves in the benchmark so you can decide route-by-route.

[08:40] Sofia: can product own a matrix of route sensitivity so we can pick which routes to optimize for cost vs latency?

[08:48] Sam: absolutely. we can provide a template and Priya can run sensitivity tests.

[09:00] 
... transcript continues with periodic checks and timestamps ...

[26:12] Priya: quick note on logs — there were a few transcription artefacts in the packet traces i want to call out: the perf counter "kernel missmatch" was actually a mis-typed counter name in our parser, not a model kernel error.

[31:45] Arman: we've started the internal postmortem doc; we'll merge Redwood's findings and post to the shared drive by EOD.

[39:05] Sam: recap of next steps: Sam to send redacted logs/SOC2 + dedicated topology; Priya to run benchmark; Arman to grant staging VPC access; Omar to schedule follow-up for week of 2027-11-30.

[39:28] Marco: thanks, appreciate the partnership.

[39:34] Lena: one last thing — can Redwood provide a short-runbook for immediate mitigation steps ops should take if we see a recurrence?

[39:42] Sam: yes, we'll attach a 1-page runbook with the logs.

[39:48] Sofia: ok good. timeline noted.

[39:55] Sam: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email and post the artifact. call ends.

[53:50] (meeting wrap and participants left)
